title: The Spirit and Scripture
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The Spirit and Scripture teaches that the Holy Spirit inspired the written Word and works through Scripture to teach, convict, comfort, guide, and sanctify God’s people.
summary: The Spirit and Scripture teaches that the Holy Spirit inspired the written Word and works through Scripture to teach, convict, comfort, guide, and sanctify God’s people.
christFocus: The Spirit glorifies Christ through Scripture by revealing His person, work, Gospel, promises, and commands. He does not lead believers away from the written Word but deeper into truth centered on Christ.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Holy Spirit is the divine author behind Scripture. The prophets and apostles did not produce God’s Word by private imagination. They spoke and wrote as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.

The same Spirit who inspired Scripture also works through Scripture. He teaches truth, brings Christ’s words to remembrance, exposes sin, strengthens faith, and equips believers for obedience.

The Spirit never contradicts the Word He inspired. Any claim to spiritual guidance that denies Scripture, weakens Christ, excuses sin, or distorts the Gospel must be rejected.

A Spirit-filled life is therefore a Scripture-shaped life. The sword of the Spirit is the Word of God, and believers need both the written Word and the Spirit’s living work to receive it rightly.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people claim the Spirit while neglecting the Bible, while others read the Bible without dependence on the Spirit. Both errors leave believers unhealthy. God joined together what we should not separate.

This doctrine protects the church from both dry intellectualism and reckless spirituality. The Spirit works through the Word to form faithful disciples of Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read Scripture with dependence on the Holy Spirit. Ask Him to open your eyes, convict your heart, strengthen your faith, and lead you into obedience. Do not follow any voice, impression, or teaching that moves you away from the Word of God and the Gospel of Christ.
